author: C Han
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | I flew with Emirates Taipei – Dubai – Geneva return. Outbound the onboard experience was a real nightmare. The flight attendants were arrogant and dismissive. Every time I tried to ask a question, they cut me off with clear impatience. I had to ask three times if I could try on the sunglasses I wanted to buy, and eventually had to stop an attendant again just to get a “no”. Then they simply forgot to bring me the product! One attendant was particularly rude — she was chatting with colleagues while ignoring my requests and even forbade me from crossing the galley to reach the restroom. The meal service was just as bad. They tried to take my tray before I had finished eating, and once I was done, no one ever came back. I was left stuck with my tray until the very last moments before landing. I couldn’t even fold my table or adjust my seat properly for arrival because the crew had completely abandoned me. On the return flight, the service was more normal. Some crew members were polite and even enthusiastic, which made the flight more pleasant. It wasn’t outstanding, but it was acceptable. Emirates used to be a great airline, but this experience left me very disappointed and  I will avoid flying with Emirates again.

author: C Yeung
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | While the overall inflight service was quite unsatisfactory, the worst and most offensive part of my experience with Emirates was the Korean customer service call center - the two most unpleasant phone service experiences I have ever encountered in my life both happened with Emirates. ​I have been struggling for over a month with an unresolved mileage accrual issue. I called the center to get this sorted out, but from the very beginning, the agent continuously talked over me and interrupted me, making it completely impossible to hold a proper conversation. When this disruptive behavior repeated, I questioned the quality of their service, asking why the consultation was being handled this way. Shockingly, the agent falsely framed my legitimate complaint as "verbal abuse" and abruptly hung up on me. ​Hoping to speak with someone else, I called back immediately, but the exact same agent answered. When I requested to be transferred to a different representative, they simply told me to call back later. I called a third time, and once again, the same person picked up. ​Utterly frustrated, I stated that I wanted to officially escalate this issue and requested the agent's name. Incredibly, the agent refused to provide their name and told me to "solve it legally." It honestly felt like there was only one person running the entire Korean call center. When I asked how many employees were even working there since I kept getting connected to the exact same person, the agent repeatedly replied, "I cannot answer that." ​This is not an isolated incident. Even before boarding, when I called to inquire about the Business Class Chauffeur-drive service, the consultation was an absolute mess and deeply unpleasant. ​Emirates desperately needs to retrain and re-educate their phone agents. I have plenty of other complaints regarding their inflight service as well, but I will not even bother mentioning them because the behavior of this call center is, by far, the most unacceptable.

author: Thao Nguyen
review_text: Not Verified | I am writing to formally express my disappointment regarding our recent Emirates Business Class experience, which fell far below the standards expected. On 08 May, Emirates cancelled the Ho Chi Minh City – Boston flight for my mother and me without providing any explanation. Subsequently, our family’s return flight from Boston to Ho Chi Minh City on 20 May was also cancelled without notice, and Emirates changed the departure date to 23 May. Our travel agency contacted Emirates multiple times via email but received little to no response. When we requested to return on 21 May instead, Emirates informed us that only two seats were available, requiring one family member to fly separately on 22 May. However, seats on the 21 May flight still appeared to be available when checked independently. What was especially concerning was that Emirates requested an additional payment of approximately VND 40,000,000 for all family members to travel together on the same flight — despite the situation originating from Emirates’ own cancellations and schedule changes. Further issues occurred during our overnight transit in Dubai. Although all required entry documents had already been submitted via email in advance as attachment, our family was still asked to wait approximately two hours for approval. At the Dubai Connect counter, staff only then reviewed the previously submitted emails and requested that the documents be forwarded again before processing could continue. Overall, the repeated cancellations without explanation, lack of communication, inconsistent information, transit handling issues, and disappointing onboard service resulted in an experience far below reasonable expectations for Emirates Business Class passengers.

author: G Quade
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | The ground experience revealed troubling gaps in professionalism and respect that are difficult to ignore.  At Montréal–Trudeau (YUL), the ticket agents were engaged in casual conversation while passengers waited in line. When I reached the counter, the agent spoke to me in a curt manner and instructed me to drop my luggage at another location, without considering my business-class status nor the protocol affiliated with it. When I requested to speak with a supervisor, I was told there was no one available. The interaction felt dismissive and unprofessional. A few minutes later, another agent quietly stepped in and demonstrated a very different approach. He appeared to understand the appropriate procedures, reviewed my passport and ticket, and recognized the oversight. He apologized on behalf of his colleague, took charge of my luggage himself, and completed the check in with calm efficiency and respect. He then went a step further and personally escorted me to the one of the lounges. The return journey from Dubai to Montréal exposed a more serious issue. At the boarding gate in Dubai, I explained to the agent that my passport would not scan on the device and that it needed to be entered manually. Instead of acknowledging this and resolving the matter calmly, she abruptly snatched the passport from my hand and muttered, under her breath, a derogatory comment. Another passenger nearby heard the remark, intervened, and pointed out how disrespectful and inappropriate her behavior was, even suggesting that if she disliked her job, she should consider another line of work. Rather than de escalating, the agent began arguing with this passenger, all while I stood waiting for my passport to be processed. The entire interaction carried a sense of rude entitlement and left a lasting feeling of discomfort. The in flight service was polished, the cabin comfortable, and the food and beverage offerings wine, sparkling options, and spirits were of a good quality.

Overall, a very disappointing experience.

author: L Almulla
review_text: ✅ Trip Verified | As a frequent flyer with Emirates, I’ve always admired the airline's reputation for exceptional service, but my recent experience in Economy has left me deeply disheartened by the stark disparity in treatment between Business and Economy class passengers. Throughout the flight, it felt as though Economy passengers were treated as an afterthought. It took an excessive amount of time to receive any service, even something as simple as water, despite pressing the call button multiple times. On one occasion, I got up to stretch my legs and was approached by a flight attendant asking if I needed help. When I explained I was just trying to get some movement, I was told to return to my seat and wait for 10 minutes until service was completed. The tone and response felt dismissive and unnecessary. Another unsettling moment occurred when I pressed the service button. A flight attendant walked past me, nodded in acknowledgment, but didn’t stop. When she finally returned, she explained she had been “counting.” While I appreciate that tasks need to be completed, ignoring a passenger’s request and providing such a response felt dismissive and unprofessional. The final incident left me utterly shocked. While refilling my water bottle, another flight attendant accidentally spilled water all over my leg. Instead of a genuine apology or assistance, his response was, “I couldn’t see.” It’s difficult to understand how such carelessness and lack of attentiveness can happen on an airline that prides itself on excellence. As someone who has experienced the polished and attentive service in Business Class, the treatment in Economy was a glaring contrast. It felt as though Economy passengers were not afforded the basic courtesy or care expected from Emirates. While I understand there are differences in service levels between classes, this experience lacked the professionalism and warmth that should be standard across all cabins. I sincerely hope Emirates addresses these inconsistencies. Loyal customers, regardless of class, deserve better treatment and respect.

author: Michael Malter
review_text: Not Verified |   My wife and I along with 2 friends took the Emirates flight from Newark, NJ to Athens in September 2023. We had never flown on Emirates but decided to give them a try over American or Delta. The numerous tv commercials with actress Penelope Cruz has subliminally triggered something that inspired me to convince my wife and friends that we should give them a try. At the time of our "economy" booking we decided to pay an additional $410 per couple for seat upgrades. We had opted to pay more for the 2 seats together rather than the sitting in a row of three or fours seat in the center of the plane. As soon as we boarded the plane and took our seats I knew the outbound flight was going to be torture. The 2 seats that we paid $205 extra for were so small with walled sides and hand rests that didn't move would have been great if we were all contortionists but unfortunately we were not. We made it to Athens 10 hours later and after a couple of good nights sleep we put this horrible memory behind us so as not to ruin our 2 week long awaited vacation. About a week into the trip we did some research on the web and decided to downgrade our return seats from the same mini seats that we flew out on and instead opted for the standard seats that were in the middle section of the plane that included 4 seats. This was a great move as our return flight was much more comfortable. When I contacted Emirates upon our arrival and asked to get back the $205 paid for the return downgraded seats, their reply was that they do not issue refunds for seat downgrades. That said, the 4 of us will never travel on Emirates again. As a postscript I want to mention that none of the 4 our us, all retired and in our late 60's are heavy or have large behinds, to the contrary, we are all smaller individuals who have never had any comparable torturous seats while flying anywhere in the world. Unless you are Penolope Cruz and get complimentary "first class" seating or opt to pay the additional thousands of dollars, stay away from Emirates.
